outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Bottleneck of Attention in the Transformer Era
outline.description: This chapter establishes the context for optimizing attention mechanisms. It explains why attention is the computational bottleneck in large language models (LLMs) and long-context applications, reviews existing optimization strategies (approximation vs. full attention), and details the hardware limitations of previous approaches on modern GPU architectures.
subtopics: Limitations of standard Attention implementation (memory bandwidth bound)
Review of FlashAttention-1 and FlashAttention-2: Core concepts and remaining inefficiencies
The rise of Hopper GPUs (NVIDIA H100): New hardware capabilities
Why current optimizations underutilize Hopper Tensor Cores (Spatial vs. Temporal efficiency)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Hardware Architecture and Execution Models
outline.description: A deep dive into the specific hardware features of the NVIDIA Hopper architecture that FlashAttention-3 exploits. This chapter equips readers with the necessary knowledge of GPU memory hierarchies, thread hierarchies, and specialized functional units required to understand the algorithmic innovations.
subtopics: GPU Memory Hierarchy: Global Memory, L2 Cache, Shared Memory (SMEM), and Registers
Thread and Warp Hierarchy: CTAs, Warpgroups, and Cooperative Thread Arrays
The Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA): Asynchronous data movement
Warp-Specialization: Producer-Consumer paradigms for hiding latencies
Asynchronous Tensor Cores (WGMMA) vs. Synchronous Ampere Tensor Cores
Low-Precision Arithmetic: FP8 capabilities, throughput gains, and accuracy trade-offs

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Core Algorithm Innovation – Warp-Specialized Asynchrony
outline.description: This chapter details the first major technical contribution: splitting workloads into producer and consumer warps. It explains how this design pattern eliminates stalling during data movement and sets the foundation for overlapping computation with memory transfers.
subtopics: The Producer-Consumer Model in Attention Kernels
Circular Buffers in Shared Memory for Pipeline Management
Register Allocation Strategies using `setmaxnreg` for Async Kernels
Case Study: Basic Forward Pass without Softmax Overlap (Algorithm Analysis)

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 4: Advanced Pipeline Optimization – Overlapping GEMM and Softmax
outline.description: Focusing on the second innovation, this chapter teaches how to bridge the throughput gap between high-performance matrix multiplication (GEMM) and low-throughput softmax operations. It introduces intra-warpgroup pipelining to achieve higher Tensor Core utilization.
subtopics: # The Throughput Gap: Why Softmax limits performance on Tensor Cores
# Breaking Sequential Dependencies within a Block Iteration
# Compiler Reordering Challenges and SASS Code Analysis
